classification.summary: BentoBox-style vault's setMasterContractApproval accepts a zero (v,r,s) signature, letting the attacker approve itself for a user and withdraw the user's RICE.

loss.notes: Migrated from legacy lossUsd/lossOther. The legacy corpus did not consistently distinguish gross from net loss or record valuation provenance.

limitations: Target identity and code history came from the v1 snapshot row originally at protocols/rice.json; no semantic revalidation was inherited.

sources.note: Onchain review: RICE vault 0xcfe0de4a50c80b434092f87e106dfa40b71a5563 created 2025-03-13T05:33:51Z (Base block 27527342) by 0x6f6f8b3b1f9ee48e315a1b7cfdb03e5550e94106, not the attack-tx sender 0x2a49c6fd18bd111d51c4fffa6559be1d950b8eff. keccak(eth_getCode) is identical at the creation and incident blocks, no EIP-1967/beacon or other implementation slot is set (slot 0, the owner, is the only non-zero slot in 0-25), and the exploit trace contains no DELEGATECALL out of the victim: the single delegatecall site in the runtime is the BoringBatchable self-call reached from batch(bytes[],bool) (selector 0xd2423b51 present; the runtime holds no address constant other than the 0xff..ff mask). Deployment basis is exact.
